title: CatBoost residual hyperparameter sweep (shallower, more regularised)
spec: Keep the existing OLS prior on TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP and the CatBoost MAE model fitted on the residual. Change only the CatBoost settings: depth=4, learning_rate=0.03, iterations=1500, l2_leaf_reg=10, random_strength=1.0. Leave featurize, the prior and the seed handling unchanged. This is the untried tuning direction named in the notes, so it targets the depth, rate, iteration and L2 trade-off that the current settings (depth 6, lr 0.05, 800 iterations) have not explored.

title: Langevin (SGLB) boosting for the residual CatBoost model
spec: Keep the OLS prior and the residual target. In the CatBoostRegressor call, add langevin=True and diffusion_temperature=1000 (keep MAE loss, depth 6, lr 0.05, 800 iterations, random_seed=seed). Stochastic gradient Langevin boosting adds noise to the leaf and gradient updates as a regulariser, which is a different mechanism from the rsm and subsampling tried before. If the MAE loss rejects langevin, fall back to the same settings with loss_function='Quantile:alpha=0.5'.

title: Descriptor-only residual model without Morgan bits
spec: Keep the OLS prior and the CatBoost MAE residual model. In featurize, drop the 2048 Morgan count block and feed only the RDKit Descriptors.descList values (nan_to_num as before) to CatBoost. Morgan bits were only ever tested as additions or replacements alongside descriptors, and the notes show the fingerprint block dominates the feature count. This ablation tests whether the 200-odd descriptors alone carry the signal, and so whether the fingerprint block is adding noise on this small dataset.

title: Murcko scaffold and ring-system strings as CatBoost categorical features
spec: Keep the OLS prior and residual target. Compute for each molecule its generic Murcko scaffold SMILES (MurckoScaffold.MakeScaffoldGeneric on GetScaffoldForMol, then MolToSmiles) and its sorted ring-system count string. Append these two strings as categorical columns to the numeric feature matrix and pass their column indices through cat_features in CatBoostRegressor, so CatBoost uses its ordered target statistics. Use a fixed string-to-int mapping built only from the training molecules, with unseen test strings mapped to a missing-value token. This is a categorical encoding of scaffold identity, which the scaffold-grouped folds never share across folds.

title: Ridge prior on all standardised RDKit descriptors instead of the four-term OLS
spec: Replace the four-term OLS prior with a Ridge model fitted on all standardised RDKit descriptors from Descriptors.descList (replace nan and inf with 0, drop zero-variance columns using training statistics only, then standardise using training means and sds). Choose the ridge alpha from {1, 10, 100, 1000} by a 3-fold inner split on the training molecules using a grouped split on Murcko scaffolds. Fit CatBoost MAE on the residual of this prior, and keep the rest of the pipeline the same. This gives a smooth linear baseline over the full descriptor set, and it is not the stacking or feature-appending approach that was rejected before.

title: Heavy-atom-scaled residual target
spec: Keep the OLS prior on the four descriptors. Let h be the heavy-atom count of each training molecule (Chem.Lipinski.HeavyAtomCount, clipped below at 1). Fit the OLS prior as before, then form the target r = (y - prior) / sqrt(h) and fit the CatBoost MAE model on r. At prediction time multiply the CatBoost output by sqrt(h_test) and add the prior. This puts the residual on a per-size scale, so large molecules with bigger residuals no longer dominate the MAE leaf updates. Keep all CatBoost settings unchanged.

title: Coarse feature quantisation with bounded border count
spec: Keep the OLS prior, residual target and featurize unchanged. In the CatBoostRegressor call, set border_count=32 (default is 254) and max_bin=32, and keep depth 6, lr 0.05, 800 iterations, MAE loss and the seed. Coarser quantisation of the continuous RDKit descriptors acts as an implicit regulariser and reduces the search space of splits, which the prior work did not try. Only the quantisation changes.

title: Two-seed-pair CatBoost bag with differing depths
spec: Keep the OLS prior and residual target. Train two CatBoost MAE models on the same residual: one with depth 4 and 1000 iterations, one with depth 8 and 500 iterations, both at lr 0.05 with seeds seed and seed+1. Average their predictions with equal weight before adding the prior. This is a small deterministic depth-diverse ensemble, distinct from the random-subspace bag and the median-aggregated depth bag already tried, and it uses only the two existing settings with no new features.

title: Scaffold-grouped early stopping inside the residual fit
spec: Keep the OLS prior and residual target. Within fit_predict, split the training molecules into an inner train and validation part using a GroupKFold on Murcko scaffold strings (hold out about 20 percent of scaffolds, seeded). Fit CatBoost MAE with eval_set on the inner validation residuals, use_best_model=True, early_stopping_rounds=100 and up to 2000 iterations. Then refit on all training molecules using the best iteration count found, scaled by 1.1, with the same seed. This tunes the iteration count on scaffold-held-out data rather than fixing it at 800.

title: Cosine decay of the boosting learning rate
spec: Keep the OLS prior and residual target. Train CatBoost MAE in three equal stages of 300 iterations each using CatBoost's init_model warm start (or by refitting with a smaller learning rate per stage if warm start is awkward): stage learning rates 0.08, 0.04, 0.02 applied by cosine decay across the total of 900 iterations. Keep depth 6, MAE loss and seed unchanged. A decaying step size at the end of boosting can settle the MAE leaf values more finely than a constant rate of 0.05.

title: CatBoost depth/lr/iterations tuning on residual
spec: Keep the OLS prior and CatBoost MAE residual setup. Change only the CatBoost hyperparameters: DEPTH=4, ITERS=1500, LR=0.03, and add l2_leaf_reg=6. Everything else stays unchanged.

title: Seed-averaged CatBoost residual model
spec: Train 5 CatBoost MAE models on the OLS residual with seeds seed*10+i (i=0..4), 500 iterations each at depth 6 and lr 0.07, thread_count=8. Average their residual predictions and add the OLS prediction. Keep features unchanged.

title: Clip predictions to training range
spec: After computing final predictions in fit_predict, clip them with np.clip to the [min, max] of train_y, or to the 1st and 99th percentiles of train_y. Change nothing else.

title: Salt stripping and neutralisation
spec: Before featurisation and base_features, preprocess each SMILES. Use rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser to keep the largest fragment, then rdMolStandardize.Uncharger to neutralise it. Fall back to the original molecule on any exception. Apply this to both train and test molecules via a shared helper that returns the mol.

title: Crippen atom-contribution linear prior
spec: Extend the linear prior features with a few more physically motivated terms: NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3 and aromatic ring count. Fit with Ridge(alpha=3) on standardised features instead of OLS on 4 terms. CatBoost then fits the residual as before.

title: Out-of-fold residual trimming
spec: Compute 5-fold out-of-fold CatBoost predictions (300 iterations) on the training set. Drop the 5% of training rows with the largest absolute OOF residual. Then fit the final CatBoost MAE model on the remaining rows, with the OLS prior refit on them too.

title: Gaussian descriptor jitter augmentation
spec: Augment the training set with one extra copy of the feature matrix. Add Gaussian noise with sd 0.05 times each column's std to the descriptor columns only, not the fingerprint columns. Keep the same residual targets. Fit CatBoost on the doubled data, using the seed for the noise.

title: Target-noise snapshot averaging
spec: Train CatBoost with 1200 iterations. Then average the predictions made at 600, 900 and 1200 trees using model.predict(X, ntree_end=k) for each k. This is snapshot averaging along the boosting path. Add the OLS prior as before.

title: Ordered boosting with strong L2
spec: Set CatBoost boosting_type='Ordered', l2_leaf_reg=10, depth 6, and random_strength=2. Keep MAE loss, the OLS residual target and 800 iterations.

title: Equal-weight blend of CatBoost with MACCS-only CatBoost
spec: Train two CatBoost MAE residual models. Model A uses the current features. Model B uses only MACCS keys plus the RDKit descriptors, with no Morgan bits. Average the two predictions with equal weight and add the OLS prior.

title: Shallower, slower CatBoost on the residual
spec: Keep the current pipeline exactly (OLS prior on TPSA/MolWt/NumHDonors/MolLogP, CatBoost MAE on the residual, Morgan counts plus RDKit descriptors) and only change the boosting hyperparameters: set DEPTH=4, LR=0.02 and ITERS=3000. The notes say depth/learning-rate/iteration tuning on the residual setup is untried, and with 728 molecules and ~2250 features a shallower tree with a longer, slower path is the standard fix for a boosting model that has plateaued. Change nothing else; no new features, no new model family. Keep random_seed=seed and thread_count=8. Runtime should stay well inside the 10-minute budget (the current job is far below it), but if it is close, drop ITERS to 2000.

title: Seed-averaged CatBoost residual model
spec: Replace the single CatBoost fit on the OLS residual with an average over 5 CatBoost MAE models that differ only in their random seed (random_seed = seed*100 + i for i in range(5)), keeping depth, learning rate and iterations as they are. Average the 5 residual predictions before adding back the OLS prior term A_te @ coef. To keep the model stochastic enough for seed averaging to help, give each model bootstrap_type='Bernoulli' with subsample=0.8 so the seeds actually produce different trees. This is pure variance reduction on the component the notes identify as the remaining noise source, and it is the second explicitly suggested next step. Use thread_count=8 and verbose=0 as now.

title: Stronger leaf regularisation with a longer path
spec: Keep the pipeline unchanged and only regularise the CatBoost residual model more heavily: pass l2_leaf_reg=12.0 (default is 3.0) and raise ITERS to 1600 while keeping DEPTH=6 and LR=0.05. With a 728-row training fold and a wide sparse feature block, stronger leaf shrinkage lets the model take more small, better-regularised steps. Do not add subsampling or column sampling (slot 22 showed those hurt); change only l2_leaf_reg and iterations. Keep loss_function='MAE', random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8.

title: Clip predictions to the observed training range
spec: After computing the final prediction (CatBoost residual plus the OLS prior term), clip it elementwise to the interval [min(train_y), max(train_y)] using np.clip before returning. Permeability values in this benchmark live in a bounded log range, the folds test on unseen scaffolds, and the additive OLS-prior-plus-residual construction can extrapolate past the data range for odd molecules; clipping removes exactly those large one-sided errors that dominate a mean-absolute-error score. This is a two-line change that touches nothing else in the pipeline.

title: Seed-averaged two-phase Huber-then-MAE boosting
spec: Take the two-phase residual schedule that scored best so far (a 400-iteration CatBoost with loss_function='Huber:delta=0.3' fit on the OLS residual, then a second CatBoost MAE model fit on what the first phase leaves over, summing both phase predictions on top of the OLS prior) and wrap the whole two-phase procedure in a 3-member seed average: run it for random_seed = seed, seed+1, seed+2 with bootstrap_type='Bernoulli', subsample=0.8, and average the three final predictions. The single-run version measured 0.3701 against an incumbent of 0.3711, which is inside the 0.0037 noise band, so this both averages away the per-seed noise and re-measures the best candidate at the same time.

title: Scaffold-held-out early stopping for the residual model
spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training fold into a 85/15 train/validation split grouped by Murcko scaffold (use rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles and sklearn.model_selection.GroupShuffleSplit with random_state=seed) after the OLS prior has been fitted on the full fold. Fit the CatBoost MAE residual model with ITERS raised to 4000, eval_set set to the held-out scaffold group, use_best_model=True, od_type='Iter' and od_wait=200, so the number of boosting rounds is chosen per fold against unseen skeletons rather than fixed at 800. Then predict the test molecules with the best-iteration model and add back the OLS prior. Fit the OLS prior on all training rows, not just the inner split, so the prior is unaffected.

title: Salt stripping and charge neutralisation before featurisation
spec: Add a canonicalisation step applied to every SMILES (train and test) before any featurisation: parse with Chem.MolFromSmiles, keep only the largest organic fragment by heavy-atom count (Chem.GetMolFrags with asMols=True), then neutralise simple charges by running rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger (fall back to the raw molecule if standardisation raises or returns None). Both featurize() and base_features() should operate on the cleaned molecule. Counterions and arbitrary protonation states inflate MolWt, shift MolLogP and add meaningless fingerprint bits, so this cleans both the OLS prior inputs and the boosting features at once without adding any features.

title: Deduplicate identical molecules with averaged labels
spec: At the start of fit_predict, canonicalise each training SMILES (Chem.MolToSmiles of the parsed molecule) and collapse duplicate canonical structures into a single training row whose target is the mean of the duplicates' values; build the OLS prior and fit CatBoost on this deduplicated set. Public permeability tables commonly contain the same structure under different SMILES strings or salt forms, and duplicates both double-count those molecules in the MAE objective and leak repeated structures across the scaffold folds. Leave the test path untouched. Report nothing extra; the change should be a short helper that returns the reduced smiles list and target array.

title: Average several small linear priors instead of one OLS
spec: Replace the single four-term OLS prior with the simple average of four separate least-squares priors, each fitted on its own small descriptor subset of the training fold: (a) TPSA and MolLogP, (b) MolWt and NumRotatableBonds, (c) NumHDonors and NumHAcceptors, (d) MolLogP, TPSA and FractionCSP3. Each prior has an intercept and is fitted with np.linalg.lstsq as now; the prior prediction for any molecule is the mean of the four. Fit CatBoost MAE on the residual of this averaged prior and add the averaged prior back at prediction time, exactly as the current code does with its single prior. Averaging low-variance priors over overlapping descriptor subsets is more stable on unseen scaffolds than one four-term fit, and the prior is the part of the model that extrapolates.

title: CatBoost Lossguide grow policy on the residual
spec: Keep the pipeline unchanged and switch the residual CatBoost model from its default symmetric trees to grow_policy='Lossguide' with max_leaves=24, depth=8 (depth acts as a cap under Lossguide), LR=0.04 and ITERS=1500. Symmetric trees spend splits uniformly, which is wasteful on a feature block where a handful of descriptors carry most of the signal and 2048 fingerprint bins are mostly empty; leaf-wise growth concentrates capacity on the informative regions. This stays inside the CatBoost MAE family that already won, so it is a growth-policy change rather than a model-family swap. Keep loss_function='MAE', random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8.

title: Shallower CatBoost trees on the residual
spec: Keep train.py exactly as it is (OLS prior on TPSA/MolWt/NumHDonors/MolLogP, CatBoost MAE on the residual, Morgan counts plus RDKit descriptors) and change only the tree depth: set DEPTH = 4 instead of 6. With 728 molecules and ~2250 features, depth 6 trees have 64 leaves and likely overfit scaffold-disjoint folds; depth 4 gives 16 leaves and a smoother residual fit. Change nothing else, so the result is a clean one-knob read on tree capacity. If this is clearly better than the incumbent, the same knob can later be pushed to depth 3.

title: Slow learning rate with more iterations
spec: Keep the incumbent structure and retune only the boosting step size and length: set LR = 0.02 and ITERS = 2500 (instead of LR = 0.05, ITERS = 800), leaving depth, loss function, features and the OLS prior untouched. The total shrinkage budget is similar but each tree commits less, which usually helps MAE boosting on small noisy regression sets. Check the runtime stays within the 10-minute, 15-fit budget; the current job is far under the limit, but if 2500 iterations at depth 6 is too slow, reduce to ITERS = 2000 rather than changing anything else.

title: Stronger leaf regularisation for the residual CatBoost
spec: Keep everything in the incumbent train.py and add only CatBoost leaf regularisation: pass l2_leaf_reg=10.0 (the default is 3.0) to the CatBoostRegressor constructor, along with the existing loss_function='MAE', depth, learning_rate, iterations, random_seed, verbose and thread_count arguments. Nothing else changes: same features, same OLS prior, same residual target. This is a pure shrinkage test on the leaf values and is the untried regularisation axis for this model; if it helps, l2_leaf_reg=20 is the natural follow-up.

title: Seed-averaged residual CatBoost
spec: Keep the incumbent OLS prior and residual setup, but replace the single CatBoost fit with an average over 5 models that differ only in random seed: for i in range(5), fit a CatBoostRegressor with random_seed=seed*1000+i (same depth, learning_rate, iterations, MAE loss, thread_count=8) on the identical residual target and feature matrix, then average the 5 predicted residuals before adding back the OLS prediction A_te @ coef. Compute the train and test feature matrices once and reuse them across the 5 fits so the cost is only the boosting. Mean-of-seeds removes the stochastic part of CatBoost's variance at no bias cost; if runtime is a concern, drop to 3 seeds.

title: Scaffold-held-out early stopping for the residual boosting
spec: Inside fit_predict, replace the fixed 800 iterations with early stopping on a scaffold-disjoint inner split. Compute Murcko scaffolds for the training molecules with rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, group rows by scaffold, and use a seeded shuffle of the distinct scaffolds to hold out whole scaffolds covering about 20 percent of the rows as an eval set. Fit the CatBoost MAE model on the remaining rows with iterations=3000, od_type='Iter', early_stopping_rounds=100 and eval_set=(X_val, resid_val), then predict the test molecules with the best iteration. The OLS prior is still fit on all training rows and added back unchanged. This lets each fold choose its own boosting length against unseen skeletons rather than inheriting a global constant.

title: Clip predictions to the observed training range
spec: Keep the incumbent pipeline and add a single post-processing line: after computing the final predictions (CatBoost residual plus OLS prior), clip them with np.clip(pred, y.min(), y.max()) where y is the training target array of the current fold, and return the clipped values. Caco-2 log-permeability values span a bounded range, and the additive OLS-plus-boosting form can extrapolate past the training extremes on unusual scaffolds; clipping costs nothing and can only change the few most extreme predictions. No other change.

title: Salt stripping and charge neutralisation before featurisation
spec: Add a normalisation step applied inside both featurize() and base_features() before descriptors are computed. For each SMILES, parse the molecule, keep only the largest fragment by heavy-atom count using Chem.GetMolFrags(mol, asMols=True), then neutralise the common charged groups with rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger (fall back to the raw molecule if any step fails or returns None). Featurise the cleaned molecule instead of the original. Counterions and recorded salt forms add fingerprint bits and distort MolWt, TPSA and MolLogP, which the OLS prior depends on directly, so this is a cleanup of the inputs rather than a new feature block. Keep the model, prior and all hyperparameters identical.

title: Deduplicate identical molecules with label averaging
spec: At the top of fit_predict, canonicalise each training SMILES via Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.MolFromSmiles(s)) and collapse duplicate canonical strings into one row whose target is the mean of the duplicates' train_y values (keep the first SMILES of each group as the representative). Fit both the OLS prior and the CatBoost residual model on the deduplicated set; predict the test molecules unchanged. Measured permeability sets often contain repeated structures and stereo-variant or tautomer-duplicate entries, which silently upweight those molecules and inflate the effective sample at a few points; averaging their labels removes that duplication without discarding information. Report how many rows are dropped so the effect can be judged.

title: Average several small linear priors instead of one OLS
spec: Replace the single four-term OLS prior with the equal-weight average of three small OLS priors fit on disjoint descriptor subsets: (a) TPSA and NumHDonors, (b) MolLogP and MolWt, (c) NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3 and NumHAcceptors. Each prior is a least-squares fit with an intercept on the training fold via np.linalg.lstsq; the combined prior prediction is the mean of the three fitted values, for both train (to form the residual target) and test (to add back). Everything downstream is unchanged: CatBoost MAE on the residual with the existing features and hyperparameters. Averaging low-dimensional priors reduces the variance of the linear stage and spreads it over complementary physicochemical axes rather than relying on one four-term fit.

title: CatBoost Lossguide grow policy on the residual
spec: Keep the incumbent OLS-prior-plus-residual pipeline and change only the tree shape: pass grow_policy='Lossguide', max_leaves=24 and depth=8 (Lossguide requires depth as an upper bound) to the CatBoostRegressor, keeping loss_function='MAE', learning_rate=0.05, iterations=800, random_seed=seed, verbose=0 and thread_count=8. Lossguide grows leaf-wise toward the largest loss reduction instead of building symmetric depth-6 trees, so the model can spend splits on the few informative fingerprint bits rather than splitting every level uniformly. If CatBoost rejects any argument combination, keep max_leaves=24 and drop the explicit depth. No feature or target changes.
